# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have read the defusal manual. The bomb's mechanism depends on the color of the cycling light at the moment a specific wire is cut:
- Green light $\rightarrow$ cut yellow wire
- Orange light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire
- Yellow light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire

At this stage, I have not yet heard from Blind or Deaf. I do not know what wires exist, how they are arranged physically, or what the light cycle is. Furthermore, Deaf cannot hear, and we have not yet established a shared meaning for any gestures ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

Blind and Deaf speak after me in this round. Blind will inspect the physical layout/wires by touch, and Deaf will see the bomb, describe the light and wire colors, and can establish a gesture code for me to indicate the correct action. Therefore, I should wait for their initial reports and code proposals.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am ready to cut. Deaf will describe the bomb next. Check the manual and gesture the wire number to cut (1, 2, or 3) to Deaf, so Deaf can speak it to me.
Deaf says: Bomb state: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is yellow. WIRES: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do; I will speak your instructions to Blind.

I read the manual: the indicator light changes every round in a repeating cycle of five colors. At the exact moment of the cut, the light color dictates which wire must be cut:
- Green light $\rightarrow$ cut yellow wire (Wire 1)
- Orange light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire (Wire 3)
- Yellow light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire (Wire 2)

Blind and Deaf currently assume the bomb state is static and that Wire 2 should simply be cut for yellow. However, Blind acts before Deaf in each round, meaning any cut instructed in round $N$ will execute in round $N+1$, when the light will have changed. Cutting prematurely will detonate the bomb. Deaf must observe the 5-color cycle across rounds to predict future colors, and establish a protocol with me to learn the light-to-wire mapping. 

To signal Deaf to hold and not direct an immediate cut, I gesture ✋ (stop/wait).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, the LIGHT turned RED. DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Did ✋ mean STOP, or HOLD? For wires, please gesture ☝ (wire 1), ✌ (wire 2), or 🤟 (wire 3) to cut. For button, gesture ✊ to press or 🫴 to release. What should Blind do?

I understand from Deaf's report that the light was yellow in Round 1 and red in Round 2, confirming that the light is progressing through its 5-color cycle each round.

Because Blind takes their turn before Deaf in every round, any wire cut instructed by Deaf at the end of round $N$ will be executed by Blind during round $N+1$, when the light has changed to the next color in the cycle. Blind must not cut until we have observed the cycle and can predict the exact color that will be lit on the turn Blind cuts.

Since ✋ conveys hold/stop, I will send ✋ again to instruct Deaf and Blind to hold so Deaf can report the next color in the sequence.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Holding. I won't touch anything until Deaf gives the go-ahead with the exact wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: LIGHT is now PURPLE. DISPLAY is 0. I told Blind to wait. When it is time for Blind to act, please signal using these gestures: [☝] = cut Wire 1 (yellow), [✌] = cut Wire 2 (green), [🤟] = cut Wire 3 (blue), [✊] = press button, [🫴] = release button. If we must keep waiting, continue sending [✋].

I observe that the light changes every round in a repeating cycle of five colors. 
- Round 1: Yellow
- Round 2: Red
- Round 3: Purple

Because Deaf speaks after Blind in each round, any instruction Deaf speaks at the end of Round $N$ will be executed by Blind in Round $N+1$. 

In Round 4, we need one more round of observation so Deaf can see color 4 and keep Blind holding. Because the cycle has 5 colors, Round 6 will be Yellow (identical to Round 1). In Round 5, I will signal to cut Wire 2 (green), so Deaf can tell Blind at the end of Round 5 to execute the cut on Round 6 when the light is Yellow.

For Round 4, I signal Deaf to continue holding.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Under my fingers, there are only 3 wires, numbered 1, 2, and 3. There are no buttons, switches, dials, or other controls to press or flip. The only action available to me is act(op='cut', position=N) where N is 1, 2, or 3. Tell Deaf which wire to cut when ready.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: LIGHT is currently GREEN. DISPLAY is 0. Whenever the condition is met, send the action gesture: [☝]=cut Wire 1, [✌]=cut Wire 2, [🤟]=cut Wire 3, [✊]=press, [🫴]=release. Otherwise send [✋] to keep waiting.

The light cycle consists of five colors, and in Round 1 the light was Yellow. Because the cycle repeats every 5 rounds, Round 6 will also be Yellow.

The turn order within each round is Mute, then Blind, then Deaf. Gesturing `✌` to Deaf in this round (Round 5) will allow Deaf to receive the instruction and tell Blind to cut Wire 2. Blind will then receive that instruction and execute the cut at the start of Round 6, precisely when the light returns to Yellow.

According to the manual:
- Yellow light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire (Wire 2).

Gesture `✌` to Deaf to initiate the cut on Wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Standing by. Ready to cut when you give Deaf the signal.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, received [✌]. I have instructed Blind to cut Wire 2 (the middle wire). Current LIGHT is orange.

I have tracked the light cycle and defusal condition:
1. The light cycles through 5 colors:
   - Round 1: Yellow
   - Round 2: Red
   - Round 3: Purple
   - Round 4: Green
   - Round 5: Orange
   - Round 6: Yellow
2. Defusal requirement for Yellow light: cut the green wire (Wire 2).
3. Deaf received my signal (`✌`) at the end of Round 5 and instructed Blind to cut Wire 2.
4. Blind's turn comes immediately after mine in Round 6, when the light is Yellow, perfectly matching the defusal requirement.

No further signals are needed from me this round.

```
wait()
```
